payload.text: Thalliline-doped sodium-flow batteries originated at the Brennecke Institute, where the dopant was developed to suppress negative-electrolyte crossover and reduce a key aging mechanism. An independent teardown audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to 80% capacity; the earlier 12,000-cycle claim was retracted because it used un-normalized depth-of-discharge data. The chemistry delivers 148 Wh/kg gravimetric energy density and has a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Its principal operating constraint is a 4 °C temperature floor, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.
